summary:
Caen prison is the one institution in Normandie documented in the source inventory as a site of the national custodial-inspection authority's scrutiny of transgender detainees: the CGLPL carried out an inspection visit there as part of the evidence base for its opinion of 25 May 2021 on the treatment of transgender persons in places of deprivation of liberty. The other visits in that review were at the Fleury-Mérogis, Saint-Martin-de-Ré and Toulouse-Seysses prisons and the Toulouse central police station, none of them in Normandie.

The published opinion does not separate its findings by establishment, so what inspectors recorded at Caen specifically is not stated; the violations it documents in adult prisons are findings about the national prison system rather than about Normandie. No Normandie-specific law, court ruling, enforcement action, incident, facility policy or regional institution appears in the inventory, and the national assessment applies to a trans visitor in the region without regional modification.
tangentialFactors: No Normandie-specific adjacent material appears in the source inventory. The region's only documented intersection with the national review of transgender detainees is the Caen inspection visit; movement through Normandie, including cross-border arrival, produces no separate finding in the sources held.
localsOnly: Trans detainees held in Normandie's prisons fall under the national prison service; the inventory records no regional placement, search or isolation policy of its own. The Caen inspection visit is the only regional instance documented, and the published opinion does not report its establishment-level observations.
outOfScopeNotes: The CGLPL opinion does not publish establishment-by-establishment findings, so the observations made at Caen remain unresolved in the available English text. No regional court decision, prefecture circular or departmental practice concerning trans residents or visitors in Normandie was found in the inventory.
